title: Hot Crepes
text: According to information gathered by my Father, Itsuki, the Bow Hero, is apparently somewhat famous. That’s strange. As I was tilting my head in confusion, my Father answered my question.
“Is it different from the memories of the future?”
“That’s right.”

“Hmm… I guess it’s probably because Motoyasu and Ren haven’t been doing much in Melromarc… maybe? When you stop hearing about a hero who used to be the talk of the town, the more low-key ones naturally start to stand out.”
“I see.”

In other words, Ren was on the front lines until the first wave, but now that he’s gone to Zeltoble out of distrust for the country, Itsuki is the only one left who’s making visible contributions. To begin with, in this loop, Itsuki has been receiving preferential treatment from the country. Now that Ren has disappeared to Zeltoble, Melromarc may have shifted its policy to give special preferential treatment to Itsuki alone.

In the future, the Three Heroes Church had been highlighting my and Ren’s exploits, but since that didn’t pan out… Itsuki naturally ended up rising to prominence. Apparently, Itsuki used to enjoy acting as a secret champion of justice. It seems the Three Heroes Church desperately spread word of his hidden exploits, which is how Itsuki’s own fame spread.

That’s just like my father. However, with unidentified “Divine Bird Saints” active all over the place, isn’t the Three Heroes Church getting pretty anxious? I’ve also heard that impostors claiming to be the Shield Hero are running amok in various regions.

“Well, this commotion isn’t really our business. Even if we were to go as the Divine Bird Saints… since Itsuki and the others have seen Yuki-chan and the others before, we’d probably be found out if we showed up.”
“That’s true.”
“But… what on earth is Itsuki’s motive for playing this ‘hero’ game? Well, I figured out during our duel that he’s the type who gets a kick out of lecturing people.”
“My father said he’s always going on and on about ‘justice’ in the future.”
“Ah… yeah. I guess he just looks up to heroes. If that’s the case… I suppose it’s not a problem?”
And so, we left the trouble to Itsuki and watched as the commotion was brought under control.

The next day, just as Father had said, word spread through town that the nobleman from the neighboring town had been defeated by Itsuki and his party. News of Itsuki’s exploits is already beginning to reach all corners of the land. I do wonder what kind of expression Itsuki has on his face—he’s impossible to hide these days. Well, I’m sure he’s probably grinning smugly with pride.
“Well then… next, let’s patrol the area along the northern border and head back for resupply.”
To celebrate our newfound freedom, my Father distributed food to the townspeople for free. Everyone was shouting words of thanks our way.
“Let’s get out of here before we run into Itsuki.”
“Well then, farewell!”
As the townspeople waved goodbye, we set off. The legend of the “Holy Bird Saint” is now becoming just as famous as the exploits of Itsuki—the Bow Hero—and his party.
And so, we headed north, almost as if fleeing from Itsuki. Apparently, there are a lot of merchants coming from the neighboring country to buy food.
“Bro, there’s a ton of bartering going on here—is that okay? Also, my jewelry isn’t selling at all.”
“Huh? Wait a sec.”
My jewelry… isn’t selling?! Nonsense! How can no one even give these sublime symbols, modeled after Filolial-sama, a second glance…? Their eyes must be rotten!
“Motoyasu, calm down. It’s just supply and demand.”

After my father calmed me down, he looked out from the carriage to survey the area. Looking around, I saw many people who were thin—perhaps from hunger. I see. So it’s just a group of people who can’t even afford to buy jewelry. In other words, it’s not Filolial-sama’s fault—it’s society’s fault.
“The customers don’t look too healthy. They’re emaciated and ragged.”
“It’s a famine, after all. That’s exactly why we’re distributing food.”
“I know, but… isn’t something off about this?”
“Bro, these folks have some kind of accent—it’s hard to understand them. Aren’t they different from the people of Melromarc?”
“Is that so? I’ll try talking to them a bit.”
After hearing Keel’s words, my Father got out of the carriage and seemed to be asking the customers what was going on.
“For now… we’ll set up a food distribution, so please calm down and come buy some once things settle down.”
My father borrowed a large pot from the villagers and began serving homemade food. While he was at it, he’s trying his hand at recreating the crepes Keel had been hoping for on a heated griddle.
“Gau!”
“Yeah, Gaelion-chan. Keep that heat up.”
Sakura-chan and the others, including Filolial-sama, are staring longingly at the food.
“I managed to get some flour through a barter deal the other day. Even if I can’t make sweet crepes just yet, I think I can make savory ones.”
“What’s the difference between savory crepes and regular crepes?”
“The batter itself is the same, but the fillings are different. Regular crepes are a dessert, but you can use meat or fish in hot crepes.”
“Huh… Are they tasty?”
Keel is watching Father cook with great interest.
“There we go… It’s done.”
After cooking the crepe batter into a round shape, Father skillfully sandwiches the cooked meat inside and hands it to Keel.
“I guess that’s it for now?”
“So this is a crepe?”
“They’re usually sweet, but we don’t have enough ingredients, so you’ll have to make do with this.”
“Got it.”
Keel takes a bite of the savory crepe. It’s a fresh dish featuring a tomato-like fruit from BioPlant sandwiched between the crepe layers.
“Hmm… it tastes good, but it’s a bit… meh.”
“You do prefer sweet things, don’t you, Keel? I’ll make you a sweet one next time, so hang in there.”
“It’s fine, it’s fine. Everything you cook is delicious, bro.”
“Really? I’ll make you a sweet crepe next time we get the chance.”
“I’m looking forward to it! But how is this any different from food where meat is wrapped in leaves?”
“Now that you mention it, that’s a tough one.”

With that, my Father gave a wry smile. He’s now presenting the soup—which they’d been preparing alongside the crepes—to the guests. Perhaps having caught their breath, the guests seemed to have regained their composure.
“Has everyone been served?”
The Father approached the guests, who were now relaxing and chatting.
“So, what exactly happened? You guys aren’t from this country, are you?”
“Well… actually, we’re from a neighboring country… We came to Melromarc—which they say has been getting wealthier lately—to stock up on food.”
“Is that so?”
“Yes. In our country, a famine coincided with a revolutionary movement; while taxes have gone down, food production is still…”
“On top of that, the victorious revolutionary army—which was supposed to have lowered taxes—broke its campaign promises and raised them instead. The country is in shambles and only getting worse…”
Well, well… So that’s why they were so emaciated. It seems there are scoundrels who deceive people everywhere in the world. It’s just like the political stories you see on TV.

“Everyone’s lamenting that the revolution was a waste of time… Even though the Bow Hero was part of the revolutionary army, how did things come to this…? If this keeps up, some other country might invade our weakened nation… But we can’t even make a living because of the famine.”
“Huh? It’s not… Itsuki. Did the Bow Hero actually take part in the revolution?”
“Yes. Apparently, he kept his name a secret, but it came to light later—it’s actually quite well-known.”
“I see… Hold on a second.”
My Father is coming over to us.
“It seems Itsuki was involved in the revolution… Is that the case in the future world as well?”
“I’ve never heard of that.”
“Really? Did things change because of our involvement?”
“Even before that, Itsuki wasn’t nearly this famous.”
“…Is someone spreading the word? In that case, would it be Melromarc or the Three Heroes Church?”
That’s the most likely explanation. Since Ren isn’t here and we’re acting as saints, it’s only natural that things would turn out this way.
